About Business Unit
IBM Cloud is the global public cloud platform from IBM, one of the most secure, scalable, and enterprise-ready cloud platforms in the world. IBM Cloud powers thousands of enterprises with Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS), Platform as a Service (PaaS), and Software as a Service (SaaS) offerings delivered across public, private, and hybrid cloud models.
Within IBM Cloud, the Network Underlay organization is responsible for designing, building, and operating the physical and software-defined network infrastructure that underpins IBM Cloud's global fleet of data centers. NetTools is the automation and tooling engineering team within Network Underlay. We build the software systems that allow network engineers to provision, configure, monitor, and manage network infrastructure at scale, across dozens of data centers globally.
The Network Automation mission within NetTools develops and operates three interconnected platforms: NCS/Axon (Network Configuration Service), the system that automates the full lifecycle of network switch configuration from initial rack bring-up to day-to-day operations; SSOT (Source of Truth) and Hivemind, the authoritative data stores for network configuration state in classic and next-generation data center environments respectively; and the associated monitoring, validation, and reporting pipelines that keep our network infrastructure compliant, observable, and reliable.
Your Role And Responsibilities
Software Developers at IBM are the backbone of our strategic initiatives to design, code, test, and provide industry-leading solutions that make the world run today. Planes and trains take off on time, bank transactions complete in the blink of an eye, and the world remains safe because of the work our software developers do. At IBM, you will use the latest software development tools, techniques, and approaches and work with leading minds in the industry to build solutions you can be proud of.
As a Back-End Developer on the NetTools Network Automation team, you will own and deliver production-grade back-end services and automation pipelines that are critical to the daily operation of IBM Cloud's network infrastructure. You will work alongside senior engineers building and evolving the Axon/NCS platform and the SSOT/Hivemind systems, taking on direct ownership of components from design through delivery.
Your Responsibilities Will Include
Implement and automate infrastructure solutions: design, develop, and maintain back-end Python microservices that implement Day-0 (initial network provisioning, Zero Touch Provisioning) and Day-2 (operational changes, firmware updates, configuration drift remediation) automation workflows. This includes owning REST API endpoints, YAML-driven input processing, and Jinja2-based configuration generation pipelines that produce switch configurations deployed across IBM Cloud data centers.
Build and maintain automated test frameworks: design, implement, and own unit, integration, and end-to-end regression tests for the Axon/NCS platform. Establishing reliable test coverage and a dedicated test environment is a key team priority, and this role will drive that work forward, including authoring test cases, identifying edge conditions, and validating end-to-end workflow correctness.
Build and set up CI/CD pipelines in OpenShift and Kubernetes environments: administer automated CI/CD systems and tools that support the development and test lifecycle of NCS/Axon services, ensuring reliable and repeatable delivery of changes to production.
Own SSOT and Hivemind integration work: design and deliver the interfaces between NCS/Axon and the SSOT/Hivemind data platforms (backed by NetBox and CockroachDB), ensuring that network context data (rack topology, port mappings, cable connections, device inventory) is reliably consumed and validated by the automation workflows.
Support the compliance and security integrity of the environment: contribute to the NCS Overhaul initiative by hardening service components, improving Docker container configuration practices, writing operational runbooks, and ensuring the platform meets IBM's security and compliance requirements.
Partner with cross-functional teams on alerting and monitoring: collaborate with Network Engineering, Data Center Operations, and program managers to develop and maintain observability for mission-critical NCS services, and provide technical escalation support for infrastructure operations teams.

Bachelor's Degree

REST API design and HTTP fundamentals: ability to design, implement, document, and consume RESTful APIs. The Axon architecture exposes Day-0 and Day-2 network build APIs consumed by multiple service teams across IBM Cloud.

description_preview:
Block is one company built from many blocks, all united by the same purpose of economic empowerment. The blocks that form our foundational teams — People, Finance, Counsel, Hardware, Information Security, Platform Infrastructure Engineering, and more — provide support and guidance at the corporate level. They work across business groups and around the globe, spanning time zones and disciplines to develop inclusive People policies, forecast finances, give legal counsel, safeguard systems, nurture new initiatives, and more. Every challenge creates possibilities, and we need different perspectives to see them all. Bring yours to Block.
The Role
At Block, we strive to build the best products in the world — including the ones our customers never see. The Justice Engineering team builds the systems Block uses to meet its legal obligations to law enforcement, courts, and government agencies.
Every month, Block receives thousands of subpoenas, civil notices, tax levies, liens, and receiverships. Getting each one right matters in both directions: responding late or incompletely exposes Block to financial, criminal, and reputational penalties, while producing more data than a request calls for breaks the trust our customers place in us. Our services automate that work end to end — identifying the right customer from a fragment of data, assembling and securely delivering records, freezing and releasing accounts, moving money, and notifying customers — for the Counsel and Compliance teams who respond to these requests on Block's behalf.
As a full stack software engineer on Justice Engineering, you will design, build, and operate these services. We're a small team with a large surface area, so the scope is real: you'll own well-scoped features end to end — from design through testing, launch, and operation — across backend services, the internal web tools our partners work in, and the pipelines that connect us to dozens of upstream systems across Block. You'll also help shape where we're going next: LLM-powered agents that read and triage incoming legal requests, a secure portal for verified external requesters, and the evolution of our tools into a platform other Block teams build on.

Partner closely with your team to design, develop, test, ship, and maintain features that automate how Block responds to legal, regulatory, and civil requests

description_preview:
At Lyft, our purpose is to serve and connect. We aim to achieve this by cultivating a work environment where all team members belong and have the opportunity to thrive.
With a billion rides per year and counting, Lyft is solving hard problems in a rapidly growing domain with a lot of data and creative solutions in Rider, Driver, Marketplace, and beyond. While traditional approaches to optimization and problem decomposition are sufficient to disrupt transportation, building a next-generation platform for low-cost, ultra-immersive transportation to improve people's lives warrants modern ML utilizing petabyte-scale data. Our highly motivated Machine Learning Engineers work on these challenging problems and define solutions to directly impact various aspects of our core business.
The Fulfillment group, within the Marketplace at Lyft, is responsible for determining what inventory can be reliably offered for a given rider session and fulfilling rider requests. The group comprises several sub-teams that generate feasible offers for riders, match rider requests with drivers, and maintain a distributed state machine to track rides and drivers from request through completion.
We are seeking a Machine Learning Engineer to join the Fulfillment team and lead the design, development, and deployment of state-of-the-art machine learning systems. This role requires a strategic thinker who can balance high-level system architecture with hands-on technical implementation. You will collaborate across teams to shape the future of ride-sharing by leveraging machine learning and data science.
Responsibilities:
Design, build, and deploy machine learning models for real-time applications, including translating state-of-the-art research into production-ready solutions
Design and implement feature pipelines, model training workflows, and serving infrastructure using Lyft's ML platform
Evaluate ML system performance against business KPIs, run experiments, and drive continuous model improvement
Partner with ML engineers, product managers, data scientists, and software engineers to align ML initiatives with business goals
Leverage data-driven insights to inform and refine ML strategies and solutions
Write production-level code and participate in code reviews to ensure quality and share knowledge across the team
Experience:
BS/MS in Computer Science, or a related field
2+ years of experience in machine learning modeling or related fields
Experience with deep learning technologies for recommendation systems, including TensorFlow, PyTorch, or similar frameworks
Understanding of statistical concepts such as hypothesis testing, regression analysis, and performance evaluation metrics for machine learning
Experience with translating state-of-the-art ML research into production systems
Proficiency in Python, Golang, or other programming language
Proven ability to tackle ambiguous problems and deliver solutions at scale
Strong communication and interpersonal skills for effective cross-functional collaboration
Benefits:
Great medical, dental, and vision insurance options with additional programs available when enrolled
Mental health benefits
Family building benefits
Child care and pet benefits
401(k) plan with company match to help save for your future

About Bridge IR
Bridge IR Co. is building the next generation of investor-relations infrastructure.
We believe investor relationships are one of a company’s most valuable assets — yet most founders still manage those relationships through fragmented CRMs, spreadsheets, email threads, meeting notes, and individual memory.
Bridge IR is building a
relationship-intelligence platform
designed to help founders understand, manage, and strengthen their investor networks. Our platform combines investor relationship management with AI-powered intelligence and scoring to surface engagement signals, identify relationship trends, and help founders understand where their attention may matter most.
We have built our initial MVP and are preparing to onboard a small group of founders into a private beta. We are now looking for an engineering intern to work directly with our Founder & CEO to help take the MVP toward
V1
.

This is not a traditional internship where you’ll be assigned small, isolated tickets.
You’ll be joining Bridge IR at an unusually early stage and will have the opportunity to
help build the product that our first customers will actually use.
As our Founding Engineering Intern, you’ll work closely with the Founder & CEO across product development, engineering, AI, and technical problem-solving. You’ll help translate customer feedback from our private beta into product improvements and contribute to the architecture and implementation of V1.
You’ll have meaningful ownership over technical projects and the opportunity to see the full startup product cycle:
Build → Launch → Learn → Iterate → Scale.
What You’ll Work On
Depending on your experience and interests, you’ll contribute to:
Product & Application Development
Help transition the existing MVP into a more scalable V1 product.
Build and improve founder-facing workflows and user experiences.
Develop account creation, authentication, onboarding, and workspace functionality.
Build investor relationship-management features and supporting infrastructure.
Improve product reliability, performance, and usability.
AI & Relationship Intelligence
Support development of Bridge IR’s AI-powered relationship-intelligence capabilities.

Help develop and refine AI-powered scoring and insights.

Help evaluate model outputs and improve the quality of product intelligence.
Beta & Product Iteration
Work directly with feedback from Bridge IR’s private-beta founders.
Identify recurring product issues and opportunities.
Translate user feedback into technical requirements.
Build, test, and iterate quickly based on real-world usage.
Data & Infrastructure

Build supporting data infrastructure and integrations.
Help establish basic product analytics and usage tracking.
Support development of internal/admin tools for managing beta users and product feedback.
What We’re Looking For
We’re looking for someone who is
curious, technically capable, entrepreneurial, and excited about building from an early stage.

learn quickly, solve problems independently, and take ownership.

description_preview:
The Department of Defense (DoD) is offering master’s and doctoral-level internship and fellowship opportunities at the U.S. Army Medical Research and Development Command – Medical Research Institute of Infectious Diseases (USAMRDC MRIID).
What will I be doing?
As an Oak Ridge Institute for Science and Education (ORISE) participant, you will engage in a collaborative learning experience alongside a multidisciplinary community of scientists and researchers. Through this fellowship, you will acquire practical, hands-on experience in designing and constructing software tools for Next-Generation Sequencing (NGS) and synthetic biology applications.
Why should I apply?
Through this research opportunity, you will learn how computational methods, hardware, and software are integrated to solve real-world biosurveillance challenges, ultimately understanding how to identify, characterize, and evaluate known and unknown biothreats. Under the guidance of an experienced mentor, you will advance your skills and knowledge navigating Linux environments, scripting languages for handling large-scale genomic data, and learning how to apply programming languages to implement complex computational models and algorithms.
Learning objectives will include:
Bioinformatics Tool Development:
Learning how to design and develop software tools to analyze large-scale, high-throughput genomics datasets generated from state-of-the-art Oxford Nanopore and Illumina sequencers.
Synthetic Biology Applications:
Gaining experience in building software tools that support synthetic biology research, including CRISPR/Cas systems, molecular engineering, and vaccine/therapeutic delivery platforms.
Advanced Computational Biology & Software Engineering:
Learning how to develop computational biology software using both traditional coding suites and emerging AI/Large Language Model (LLM) tools.
Genomic Sequencing & Bioinformatics:

About Oden:
Manufacturing is undergoing its fourth industrial revolution, with factory operations increasingly driven by real-time applications that combine process and context data with advanced ML and AI algorithms. This is unlocking a staggering opportunity to improve the efficiency and productivity of existing manufacturing processes.
As a Manufacturing AI company, Oden is at the forefront of this revolution. We combine large-scale data processing architectures and advanced AI and ML algorithms within the Oden platform so manufacturing operations teams can continuously monitor, analyze, and optimize their production, across a diverse set of processes and conditions. Our goal is to maximize efficiency, sustainability, and competitiveness in the manufacturing domain - to help True Makers Make Things Better!
Culture
We obsess over customers. Everything we do is to create profound results and delight for our customers. Every Viking cares about the purpose of the product and company, and prioritizes work based on customer end results. When in doubt, we go to the Gemba – we’re happy to put on steel toe boots and hit the factory floor to work with the production manager.
We move fast and follow through – we live by transparent and scientific thinking, act with urgency, and put in the work to find the best ideas with those around us.
We elevate each other by giving and receiving direct, honest feedback and holding ourselves and others to a high standard to help the team rise, deliver, and win together.
“Be True Makers to Serve True Makers.” We’re building a community that fuels innovation and accelerates our pace and impact. We always ask if there’s a better way to do something, even if it's unconventional – then we try it. We aim for bold yet simple solutions that cut through complexity and drive meaningful progress.
The Solutions Engineer is a core member of Oden’s post-sales team, responsible for delivering the technical work that makes our enterprise manufacturing customers successful. The post-sales team includes Solutions Managers, Customer Success Engineers, and other Solutions Engineers depending on the size and complexity of the account. On smaller accounts, you’ll be the main technical resource, working in close partnership with the Customer Success Engineer who coordinates the customer relationship and adoption side. On larger, multi-site programmes, you’ll go deep on technical execution as part of a team coordinated by a Solutions Manager.
As an engineer in a technical role, you will design and build integration solutions that allow the Oden platform to connect to different factory systems and APIs. You will work closely with the Oden Data Science team to design and build AI and ML based solutions to customer problems, configure and deploy these solutions within the Oden platform, and drive the technical outcomes that keep deployments on track and customers seeing value. Strong data analytical skills - to be able to interpret data from the customer, triage issues, understand failure modes and deliver fixes are key to the role. You will also be expected to work closely with the core product and platform engineering team to set up requirements, and drive updates and improvements to the product capabilities.
This role requires strong data handling and analysis fundamentals, attention to detail, technical depth — Python, Golang, SQL, APIs, ETL pipelines, use of AI agents for coding, analysis, and automation — alongside the customer-facing instincts to build trust with a plant manager and the product sensibility to translate what you see on the floor into meaningful input for Product and Engineering.
Responsibilities
Customer Partnership
Serve as the primary technical resource on assigned accounts — from discovery and solution design through deployment, integration, and ongoing technical support
Work in close partnership with the Solutions Manager and Customer Success Engineers, ensuring technical and relationship responsibilities are clearly covered across the team
Build trusted relationships with customer technical leads, IT teams, and manufacturing operations stakeholders — becoming the go-to for technical questions, troubleshooting, and integration guidance
Proactively surface technical risks and blockers early, and pull in the right internal expertise when needed to keep deployments on track
Technical Solution Design and Implementation
Collaborate with Sales, Data Science, and Product Engineering to understand customer use cases, data integration requirements, and technical constraints given the different data models across customers and Oden.
Design and implement technical solutions that integrate relevant data sources to Oden’s cloud endpoints, including system configurations, data architecture, and integration requirements. Have a strong understanding of the correctness and performance (latency/uptime) for every deployed integration. These are complex distributed systems and being able to understand their interactions and points of failure is critical.
Oversee integration with existing manufacturing systems including ERP, MES, and QMS platforms; manage dependencies, sequencing, and technical risks across systems
Develop, maintain, and improve connector libraries that interface Oden with common manufacturing and enterprise systems — building reusable tooling that makes future deployments faster and more repeatable. Collaborate with the product and platform engineering team to integrate these libraries into the product.
Work with Data Science to design the solution for the customer problem, including the use of AI and ML models. Lead the technical implementation of Oden solution — configuring and customising the platform, building models and detectors, and combining them with alerts and recommendations to align with customer workflows, processes, and business rules and drive value.
Actively develop implementation planning on your accounts — scope, configurations, timelines, and

description_preview:
About SecurityScorecard:
SecurityScorecard is the global leader in cybersecurity ratings, with over 12 million companies continuously rated, operating in 64 countries. Founded in 2013 by security and risk experts Dr. Alex Yampolskiy and Sam Kassoumeh and funded by world-class investors, SecurityScorecard’s patented rating technology is used by over 25,000 organizations for self-monitoring, third-party risk management, board reporting, and cyber insurance underwriting; making all organizations more resilient by allowing them to easily find and fix cybersecurity risks across their digital footprint.
Headquartered in New York City, our culture has been recognized by Inc Magazine as a "Best Workplace,” by Crain’s NY as a "Best Places to Work in NYC," and as one of the 10 hottest SaaS startups in New York for two years in a row. Most recently, SecurityScorecard was named to Fast Company’s annual list of the
World’s Most Innovative Companies for 2023
and to the Achievers 50 Most Engaged Workplaces in 2023 award recognizing “forward-thinking employers for their unwavering commitment to employee engagement.” SecurityScorecard is proud to be funded by world-class investors including Silver Lake Waterman, Moody’s, Sequoia Capital, GV and Riverwood Capital.
About the Role:
We are looking for a GTM Engineer to help us build the next generation of systems, automations, and AI-powered workflows for our go-to-market teams.Reporting to the Principal GTM Systems Architect, you will work across Salesforce, Agentforce, Workato, Zapier, Claude Code, and the broader GTM technology stack to turn business problems into practical, scalable solutions.
This is a hands-on builder role. You will partner with teams across Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, Support, Finance, and Revenue Operations to understand where work is getting stuck, identify opportunities to improve it, and build solutions that people actually use. The right person will have a strong Salesforce foundation, solid development credentials, experience with object-oriented programming, and a genuine interest in how AI is changing the way GTM teams operate.
What You'll Do:
Build and improve AI-powered workflows and agents using Salesforce Agentforce.
Develop Salesforce solutions using Flow, Apex, custom objects, permissions, APIs, and other platform capabilities.
Design and implement scalable solutions using object-oriented programming principles.
Build integrations and automations across Salesforce and the GTM stack using Workato and Zapier.
Use Claude Code and other AI development tools to prototype, build, test, and troubleshoot solutions.
Connect systems and data through APIs, webhooks, middleware, and native integrations.
Work directly with GTM teams to understand their processes and turn recurring pain points into technical solutions.
Implement enrichment and signal-detection tooling, such as Clay or similar platforms.
Design and manage signal-based and buyer-trigger analytics, including opportunity scoring and routing.
Develop and manage data models and scoring layers for customer propensity, ICP attribution, and lead and account scoring.
Support AI use cases across prospecting, account research, pipeline management, quoting, customer success, support, renewals, and internal knowledge.
Test and monitor agents and automations to ensure they are reliable, secure, and working as intended.
Troubleshoot issues across Salesforce, Agentforce, integrations, automation logic, permissions, and data.
Document and communicate what you build so solutions can be maintained and improved overtime.
Participate in sprint planning, technical design, testing, releases, and post-launch iteration.
Measure whether the solutions you build are improving adoption, efficiency, data quality, or business outcomes.
Required Qualifications:
Three or more years of experience in GTM Engineering, Salesforce, Business Systems, Revenue Operations Systems, or a similar technical role.
Strong hands-on Salesforce experience, including Flow, data modeling, permissions, APIs, automation, and production support.
Proven development experience and an understanding of object-oriented programming concepts such as classes, inheritance, and modular design.
Experience building or configuring solutions with Salesforce Agentforce.
Hands-on experience building automations and integrations in Workato and Zapier.
Experience integrating Salesforce with other business systems using APIs, webhooks, and middleware.
Working knowledge of JSON, REST APIs, authentication, data mapping, and integration troubleshooting.
Experience with Apex, Python, JavaScript, or another object-oriented language used to extend low-code platforms.
An understanding of how Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, and other GTM teams operate.
Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to work through ambiguous requirements.
Clear communication and documentation skills.
A practical mindset. You care about whether something works for the business, not just whether it is technically interesting.
Preferred Qualifications:
Salesforce Data Cloud, Revenue Cloud, Service Cloud, or Slack.
Claude Code or another AI-assisted development environment.
Model Context Protocol, tool calling, retrieval-augmented generation, or semantic search.
Git, Gearset, Salesforce CLI, Postman, or similar development and release tools.
GTM platforms such as Clay, LeanData, Gainsight, ZoomInfo, 6sense, or Clari.
Experience with signal-based selling, buyer-intent data, enrichment, opportunity scoring, or propensity modeling.
Salesforce certifications related to platform development, Agentforce, or Data Cloud.
You do not need experience with every tool in our environment. You should be comfortable learning new technologies and choosing the right approach for the problem, whether that means configuring Salesforce, building a Workato recipe, creating a Zap, calling an API, or writing code.
Benefits:
Specific to each country, we offer a competitive salary, stoc

Description
The Advanced Computing Lab at the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), Science and Technology Directorate (S&T) is seeking passionate self-starters to participate in research and development (R&D) for the next generation of cyber-physical simulation and defense. This next generation requires moving beyond traditional, static information technology (IT) security to model the dynamic physical consequences of cyber-attacks on the nation’s most critical infrastructure—including power grids, water systems, natural gas pipelines, and other infrastructure like seaports.
This appointment is hands-on, and the selected participant should have a background that allows them to understand data and multiphysics models of complex systems and translate them into scalable, high-performance code. Participants will have the opportunity to learn to apply and hone these skills and acquire additional ones as they work on real-world problems.
Examples Of Research Areas
Cyber-Physical Modeling: Researching and developing high-fidelity virtualized environments, including emulation and simulation of industrial control systems, communication layers such as TCP/IP and peer-to-peer protocols, intelligent electronic devices, and physical simulators of critical infrastructure systems. This includes modeling how digital commands and network activity interact with physical infrastructure, such as pipeline pressure, grid stability, or voltage behavior.
Applied Mathematics to Code: Translating complex physical equations (differential equations) into modular, reusable software components to build scalable digital twins.
Generative AI: Application of Large Language Models (LLMs) to generate synthetic data for digital twins and their role in supporting cyber-physical systems.
Advanced AI & Analytics: Exploring the intersections of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and physics, including diffusion models, Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs), Neural Ordinary Differential Equations (Neural ODEs), and broader LLM applications.
Knowledge Graphs: Developing Knowledge Graph architectures to map complex interdependencies and uncover insights across multi-sector systems. Explore how knowledge graphs can support digital twins.
Location
Washington, D.C. or remote from within the United States. The location will be coordinated with the participant's mentor.
Provisions
Selected participants will receive a competitive stipend for living and other expenses during this appointment as determined by DHS. Stipends are determined by the participant's academic standing, discipline, and professional background.
Participants May Also Be Eligible To Receive
Health insurance allowance.
Reimbursement for travel expenses.
Travel/training allowance for professional development and travel to professional meetings, such as conferences.
Duration
Generally, appointments are for one year and may be extended based upon project needs and funding availability.
Nature of the Appointment
You will not enter into an employee/employer relationship with ORISE, ORAU, DHS or any other office or agency. Instead, you will be affiliated with ORISE for the administration of the appointment through the ORISE appointment letter and Terms of Appointment.
Security Clearance
Although you will not enter into an employee/employer relationship with ORISE, ORAU, DHS or any other office or agency, you must have or be eligible to obtain and maintain a security clearance for the duration of your appointment. It is expected that after completing the necessary application for clearance a fitness determination will allow participation to begin with unclassified material, while awaiting a clearance.
The successful applicant(s) will be required to comply with Environmental, Safety and Health (ES&H) requirements of the host facility, including but not limited to, COVID-19 requirements (e.g., facial covering, physical distancing, testing, vaccination).

To qualify for this opportunity you must,
Be 18 years of age or older at time of application.
